name: Pagination
summary: Lets people move between the pages of a long list, with the current page marked.
description: A pagination splits a long list of results into pages and lets people go to a page by its number, or to the previous and next ones. It shows which page is current. The pages are links: each one has a destination, so the browser handles history and focus. Which page numbers to show (all, a window around the current one) is the application's choice: the component renders the list it is given.

anatomy.description: Root: a navigation landmark named Pagination. Carries the size and the states forced for review.
The list of links: previous, the pages, next.
One page: its link, or the current page. Takes the states of its link.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: The page number, or an ellipsis for skipped pages.

properties.name: Destination
properties.description: Where the page link goes. Ignored for the current page.

properties.name: Current
properties.description: Whether this is the current page: shown filled, not linked, exposed as current.

anatomy.description: The link to the previous page, with a chevron and the word Previous; disabled on the first page.
The link to the next page, with the word Next and a chevron; disabled on the last page.
The link to a page, or the current page as text marked current, or a previous or next link without destination, disabled.
Chevron glyph of the previous and next links. Hidden from assistive technology; the words carry the meaning.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Height of the links and text size.

properties.name: Landmark label
properties.description: Name of the navigation landmark, so it is told apart from the other navigation regions.

properties.name: Pages
properties.description: The page links to show, in order, one of them current.

properties.name: Previous page
properties.description: Destination of the previous link; without one (the first page) the link is disabled.

properties.name: Next page
properties.description: Destination of the next link; without one (the last page) the link is disabled.

states.description: A page link: text on a transparent background.
Pointer over a link: the subtle neutral tint. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Pointer, finger or key pressed down on a link: the next tint.
Keyboard focus on a link. Shows the shared focus ring around it; pointer focus shows none.
The current page (the entry's current property): filled with the accent neutral color, not a link, exposed as the current page.
A previous or next link without destination: dimmed, not focusable, exposed as disabled.

notes: Previous, the pages and next sit on one row and wrap when the space runs out, separated by container.gap.
Each link is a square of the size at least, wider when its label is; previous and next show a chevron and a word.

name.text: The landmark is named by its label property (aria-label on the web), Pagination by default. Each link is named by its text (the page number, Previous, Next; the chevrons are hidden); the current page is marked as such.

keyboard.action: Moves focus through the enabled links in order: previous, the pages, next. The current page and a disabled link are skipped.

guidelines.text: A pagination is a navigation landmark with a label, holding a list of links, one of them marked as the current page; the previous and next links say so in words.

Use a nav element with aria-label="Pagination" holding a list; page links are native links, the current page a span with aria-current="page", and a previous or next link without destination a span with role="link" and aria-disabled="true", not focusable.
Give each navigation landmark of a page a unique label, so people moving between landmarks can tell the pagination from the main navigation.
Each link's purpose is clear from its text in the context of the landmark (page 3 of the results); keep the pagination in the same place on every page of the set.
The current page is distinguished by its fill and by not being a link, and exposed as current, never by color alone; a disabled link is dimmed and exposed as disabled.

Link text contrasts 19.07:1 (light) and 11.27:1 (dark) with the default surface and 11.71:1 and 9.16:1 on the hover tint; the current page 16.29:1 and 13.84:1 on its fill. Disabled links are inactive and exempt.
The chevrons are decorative and hidden with aria-hidden="true": the words Previous and Next name the links.
A visible focus indicator appears around the focused link; the focus ring contrasts 5.79:1 (light) and 12.80:1 (dark) with the surface.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.
Every link is at least 32 x 32 CSS pixels, above the minimum target.
A page control displays a row of indicators, one per page in a flat list, the current one solid: the iOS counterpart for a few pages; numbered links remain for long lists.
Color transitions of the links are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

decisions.text: Pages are links with destinations, in a navigation landmark named Pagination; the current page is not a link and is exposed as current; previous and next are links with a visible word, disabled without destination. The component renders the pages it is given and decides nothing about which numbers to show.
decisions.rationale: Links give history, focus and announcements for free; a pagination made of buttons needs script.

decisions.text: Links are primary text on a transparent background, tinted with the subtle neutral fill on hover and its hover step on press (the Button's ghost tints); the current page is the accent neutral fill with its on-accent text; disabled links take the disabled text color.
Two sizes from the space scale: small (32 px links, 14 px text, 20 px chevrons) and medium (40 px, 16 px, 24 px, the default), with 4 px corners and 4 px between links.
